name: Name
body: Battle Forge is a monthly series that presents a new WARMACHINE scenario in each installment. Battle Forge scenarios emphasize the narrative unfolding over the course of a game and may be asymmetrical, uneven, and even somewhat experimental because the goal of Battle Forge is to create a sandbox toolset that allows for creative scenario generation and new, story-worthy experiences with WARMACHINE! Players are encouraged to modify Battle Forge scenarios in any way that makes the scenario more appropriate for their army collections and their available terrain resources. Most important of all, have fun! And if you find a better way to do something with a scenario that results in a better experience for you, let us know at feedback@privateerpress.com, so we can try it, too!

name: Name
body: Following are the key terms that will be repeated in many Battle Forge scenarios:

name: Name
body: Many scenarios utilize objectives. An objective can either be a terrain piece, a marker, or a zone designated on a terrain piece or on the map.

name: Name
body: Objective Markers are impassable terrain features and should be represented on the table with markers that are at least 20 mm in diameter. Unless otherwise specified, all Objective Markers used in a scenario should be the same size.

name: Name
body: To have more models in an area than your opponent does.

name: Name
body: An area or objective is contested if both players have models in the area or in scoring proximity to the objective at a time when scoring would take place. An area or objective is uncontested if only one player has models in the area or in scoring proximity to the objective when scoring would take place.

name: Name
body: The zone or the area of a terrain feature is held when a player occupies the area with two or more models, uncontested.

name: Name
body: An objective terrain piece or marker is secured when a player has two or more models within 1" of the objective, uncontested.

name: Name
body: Battle Forge victories can be determined by either achieving the goals of the scenario or through Victory Points, scored in a variety of ways throughout playing a scenario. Turn limits on scenarios put pressure on players to succeed within a set amount of turns, and Victory Points provide the means to determine victory when neither player has completed the primary objective of a scenario.

name: Name
body: In addition to its standard rules, each Battle Forge scenario has two random tables that add additional Victory Point-scoring opportunities for players that vary each time the scenario is played. Mission Modifiers add additional scoring opportunities based on the position of a player’s models on the table. Achievements add additional scoring opportunities based on a player’s actions taken on the battlefield. Players should roll a d6 to randomly determine Mission Modifiers and Achievements before the beginning of a game, or players can choose them at will if all players agree. It is recommended that only one Mission Modifier and one Achievement should be in effect during any match (unless you really want to get crazy).

name: Name
body: If a player makes an attack that destroys one or more friendly models, that player’s opponent gains 1 Victory Point. If a player makes an attack and destroys their own Leader model, that player immediately loses the match.

name: Name
body: In addition to objectives, Battle Forge scenarios will routinely draw on the following terrain elements. Dimensions provided are approximations, and you should feel free to substitute any terrain pieces you have available as necessary. Use the resources you have available to get close enough to maintain the spirit and intention of the scenario.

name: Name
body: An obstacle with an approximate footprint of 3/4" x 4". Barriers provide cover.

name: Name
body: Obstructions with an approximate footprint of 4" x 4".

name: Name
body: Forest areas with an approximate footprint of 5" in diameter.

name: Name
body: An obstacle with an approximate footprint of 2" x 2". Small obstacles provide cover.

name: Name
body: An elevated platform at least 1" above the table, such as a hill or terrace. Plateaus can possess multiple areas at different heights that models can be placed on, but the areas must be level to prevent models from falling over. If a model cannot be placed on a level area without risk of falling off, it cannot occupy that area. Models cannot be placed on slopes, and we recommend that plateau terrain with sloped surfaces not be used. Plateau, Small—A plateau platform with a footprint approximately 6" in diameter and a level surface(s) at least 1" above the table that is large enough for five 30 mm models to be placed on. Plateau, Large—A plateau with a footprint approximately 6" to 12" in diameter and a level surface(s) at least 1" above the table that is large enough for five 40 mm models to be placed on.

name: Name
body: An area of shallow water approximately 6" in diameter.

name: Name
body: An area of rubble approximately 6" in diameter.

name: Name
body: A 3" x 5" trench template.

name: Name
body: The two scenarios in this installment of Battle Forge utilize the Guard Tower terrain feature. If you don’t have a Guard Tower (or Guard Towers), feel free to substitute or improvise other suitable terrain pieces to stand in for the Guard Towers, but still use the Guard Tower rules.

name: Name
body: Two armies clash in a desperate struggle for control over a fortified strategic pass critical for maintaining supply lines through a treacherous region. Whoever holds the towers will hold the pass, and whoever holds the pass will determine who and what can come and go.

name: Name
body: "None Shall Pass" is designed for 50- and 75-point forces.

name: Name
body: "None Shall Pass" ends after six rounds.

name: Name
body: Players battle over control of two guard towers flanking a road. Destroying the guard towers is not an option

name: Name
body: Secure both the Guard Towers for two consecutive turns or secure both of them at the end of the sixth round.

name: Name
body: This scenario uses 4 small hills, 6 small forests, 2 Guard Towers, 4 medium rubble fields, 2 large ponds, 4 small walls, and 4 small obstacles on the table as shown on the map below. If you don’t have this exact assortment of terrain, use what you have to create a diverse environment with an emphasis on terrain that blocks line-of-sight across long distances. The essential elements of the layout are the two buildings 6" apart at the center of the map, which are the primary objectives of the scenario. To the left and right of these buildings should be an assortment of difficult-to-navigate terrain. It is also ideal to have terrain that restricts movement between the deployment zone and the buildings so that the buildings are not easily rushed by an entire army.

name: Name
body: Bonfire — A trooper model within 1" of a Guard Tower can make a special action to place a 20 mm bonfire token in base contact with the Guard Tower. Only one bonfire can be placed in contact with each side of the Guard Tower. Smoke Out — If there are two bonfires in base contact with a Guard Tower during either player’s Maintenance Phase, all models occupying the Guard Tower must exit the tower. Models that must exit the tower but cannot exit the tower for any reason are destroyed. Snuff — If your unit secures a bonfire token, you can remove that token from the table. Starting on the second player's second turn, a player securing a Guard Tower gains 1 Victory Point for each Guard Tower secured. If a player destroys a Guard Tower, that player loses the match.

name: Name
body: Roll once on both the Mission Modifiers and Achievement tables.

name: Name
body: Roll a d3 to determine the Mission Modifier for this match: 1. Eye in the Sky— Gain 1 victory point on any turn that you destroy the last model in a unit, a solo, or a cohort model with an attack from a model on the top floor of a Guard Tower. 2. Tower of Power— Gain 1 victory point if you have models on the top floor of a Guard Tower at the end of your opponent’s turn. 3. Surrounded— Gain 1 victory point if you have models on both your side of the table and your opponent’s side of the table each within 6" of the Guard Towers and your opponent does not have models within both of the same areas as well.

name: Name
body: Roll a d3 to determine the Achievement for this match. 1. Homesteader— Gain 1 victory point the first time when you move models into an unoccupied Guard Tower. 2. Firefighter— Gain 1 victory point the first time you remove a bonfire from the battlefield. 3. Roughrider— Gain 1 victory point the first time one of your models or units crosses the midpoint line between your opponent’s side and your side by moving through rough terrain.

name: Name
body: Victory conditions are checked in the following order: Decisive Win: At the end of six rounds, if a player is securing both Guard Towers, that player wins the match. Point Advantage Win: At the end of any of the second player’s turns, a player with 5 or more victory points than their opponent wins the match. Last Leader Win: At the end of any of the second player’s turns, a player with the last Leader model in play wins the match. Victory Point Win: If neither player has a Leader in play at the end of any of the second player’s turns, the player with the most victory points wins the match. At the end of six rounds, the player with the most victory points wins the match.
